## Description {#details}

C++ header file with declarations for the µTest++ type trait utilities and metaprogramming support.

This header provides the declarations for the type trait utilities and metaprogramming constructs used within the µTest++ framework. It defines templates and variable traits for function traits, type lists, identity, value wrappers, compile-time checks for container and floating-point types, and type convertibility.

These utilities underpin advanced template programming, type deduction, and compile-time introspection, supporting the flexible and type-safe design of the framework. The provided traits and wrappers enable expressive and generic handling of types, values, and callable objects, facilitating robust and maintainable test code.

All definitions reside within the <code><Link to="/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits">micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits</Link></code> namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.

All header files are organised within the <code>include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus</code> folder to maintain a structured and modular codebase.

This file is intended for internal use within the framework and should not be included directly by user code.

  labels = {["constexpr", "static"]}>
Variable template to determine if a type provides an <code>epsilon</code> member.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">The type to be checked for the presence of an <code>epsilon</code> member.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<ParametersListItem name="false">otherwise.</ParametersListItem>

The <code>has&#95;epsilon&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> defines a member named <code>epsilon</code>. This trait is determined at compile time using SFINAE and the <code>is&#95;valid</code> utility, and is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable generic handling of types that represent floating-point values or require precision control.

Variable template to determine if a type is a floating point type.

</ParametersList>

<ParametersList title="Return Values">
<ParametersListItem name="true">if <code>T</code> is a floating point type.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="false">otherwise.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
The <code>is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> is a floating point type (<code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, or <code>long double</code>). For all other types, it evaluates to <code>false</code>. This trait is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable type-safe handling and specialisation for floating point types in template metaprogramming.

Specialisations are provided for <code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, and <code>long double</code>, each evaluating to <code>true</code>.

<Link id="l00542" /><CodeLine lineNumber="542"><Highlight kind="normal">    </Highlight><Highlight kind="comment">/&#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00543" /><CodeLine lineNumber="543"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @brief Function template to determine if one type is convertible to</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00544" /><CodeLine lineNumber="544"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; another.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00545" /><CodeLine lineNumber="545"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00546" /><CodeLine lineNumber="546"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @tparam From The source type to be checked for convertibility.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00547" /><CodeLine lineNumber="547"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @tparam To The target type to which conversion is tested.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00548" /><CodeLine lineNumber="548"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00549" /><CodeLine lineNumber="549"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @param (int) Dummy parameter used for overload resolution.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00550" /><CodeLine lineNumber="550"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @retval true if &#96;From&#96; is convertible to &#96;To&#96;.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00551" /><CodeLine lineNumber="551"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00552" /><CodeLine lineNumber="552"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @details</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00553" /><CodeLine lineNumber="553"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; The &#96;is&#95;convertible&#96; function template checks, at compile time, whether</Highlight></CodeLine>

<Link id="l00555" /><CodeLine lineNumber="555"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; achieved using SFINAE and is primarily used as an implementation detail</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00556" /><CodeLine lineNumber="556"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; for the &#96;is&#95;convertible&#95;v&#96; variable template within the µTest++</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00557" /><CodeLine lineNumber="557"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; framework.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00558" /><CodeLine lineNumber="558"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00559" /><CodeLine lineNumber="559"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; If the conversion is valid, this overload is selected and returns</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00560" /><CodeLine lineNumber="560"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; &#96;true&#96;.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00561" /><CodeLine lineNumber="561"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;/</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
